NR-962.title: CALL: rivers divide provinces much less once the fill crosses the settled line, and the river cost never made a river divide its banks
NR-962.source: BL-1150 (province fill crosses the settled line), lane adc45b16, cold review 2026-09-27
NR-962.what: Ruling 2 (PROVINCES.md): 'Boundaries are rivers and elevation difference.' After BL-1150, on the home body a river edge is a province border 14.92% of the time against 12.13% for plain ground (1.23x), down from 44.52% vs 27.73% (1.61x); on 3 of 16 shipped seeds rivers divide no more than plain ground. Mechanism (review, from the code): the settled line used to be a 100% border, and river courses cross that line more than plain ground does (colonisation prices river tiles as corridors, and streams cross unfarmable ground), so removing the lock removed borders that happened to sit on rivers. DEEPER, PRE-EXISTING: the river cost (+40, k_province_river_edge_cost) is charged on the step ALONG a course, from a course tile to its downstream neighbour (river_generation.cpp ~223-230, province.cpp ~212-213). So the fill pays to travel along a river, and crossing from one bank to the other through a course tile over two plain edges costs nothing. A river never divided its banks; borders 'on river edges' cut the river across. The river row (C2a) likely passes even with the river cost at 0 -- the lane is running that mutation now. ON THE SHIPPED WORLDS (fix round 67118846, 16 seeds pooled, home body): rivers were already weak before BL-1150 -- a river edge is a border 1.19x as often as plain ground on main (41.61% vs 34.87%) and 1.18x after (29.63% vs 25.15%); the 1.61 -> 1.23 drop is the harness world only. Per seed, rivers divide no more than plain on 1 seed on main (38) and 3 after (12, 37, 38). The river cost does matter on shipped worlds: at cost 0, 7 of 16 go red (the harness world still passes, so its row never tested the cost). The geometry is confirmed from the code: the +40 is paid travelling along a course; crossing bank to bank costs nothing extra.
NR-962.why_it_matters: Rivers as borders is a named property of the map, and as built it holds only by accident of where centres and the settled line fall.
options: A: accept the weaker river borders as the cost of a centre holding its whole ground
B: make a river divide its banks -- the fill pays to CROSS a course (stepping onto or off it across the flow), not to travel along it; measured first
C: raise the river cost on today's geometry
D: other
NR-962.recommendation: B: rivers divide banks as ruling 2 says -- on shipped worlds they barely divide at all today (1.19x plain), with or without BL-1150. BL-1150 can merge first; the red C13 river row is this call.
NR-962.resolution: RULED (Ben, 2026-10-01, the open calls form): B: a river divides its banks -- the fill pays to cross a course, not to travel along it; measured first, with a row that fails at river cost 0. PROVINCES.md; BL-1156 (rivers divide banks).

NR-968.title: CALL: how to break the price cycle that silences consuming markets three ticks in four (BL-1186)
NR-968.what:
With nothing listed (the shelf is not counted as supply: shelf_supply_ticks = 0), a bid aims at 10x base and the price moves halfway; above the 2x reservation ceiling BL-1172 removes the want entirely so the price can ease. Together every market on a landmass cycles 1.6x -> 5.8x -> 3.4x -> 2.2x in step: a consuming market bids one tick in four, so a hauler sees zero demand at the destination and ships nothing, and a site whose own shelf holds steel may not draw it (BL-1183). Routing fixes (ports, partial LP sends) are going ahead regardless; this is the price half.

UPDATE (2026-10-04, the BL-1193 diagnosis): the household bid is a pricing pull that never takes goods off a shelf, so household-good shelves only grow - the premise behind holding k at 0 until spoilage. BL-1196 (households consume) makes households drain the shelf as POPULATION.md already says. The same diagnosis finds the cycle's worst case: households bid water nobody lists, water sits at 10x everywhere, and the makers of clean water and medical supplies may not draw their own input. Option B (keep the over-ceiling want visible) would make that lock worse.
NR-968.why_it_matters: Without it, even routable surplus moves one tick in four; with it, shortages price into shipments. Option B partly reverses your 2026-10-03 ruling (BL-1172), so it is yours.
options: A: count the shelf as supply (shelf supply k > 0) - your 2026-10-03 path - which brings BL-1179 (shelf spoilage) forward into wave 1, since k was to follow it
B: an over-ceiling draw still registers its want (the price sees it) but does not buy - a partial reversal of BL-1172
C: haulers read a separate unmet-want register over several clears; the price still eases as BL-1172 wants (a new saved field)
D: other
NR-968.recommendation: A, built together with BL-1196 (households consume from the shelf): with households draining shelves, a shelf counted as supply no longer only grows, so k > 0 is safe without waiting for spoilage; BL-1179 (shelf spoilage) stays as the drain for goods no household eats. Not B.
NR-968.resolution: RULED (Ben, the market calls form, 2026-10-05): option A - the shelf counts as supply (k > 0) and BL-1179 (shelf spoilage) is brought forward into wave 1. Spoilage settled in MARKETS.md (2026-10-05, on Ben's delegation; NR-970); k is set by measurement on the market viability gate once the shelf drains (households eat via BL-1196, and it spoils).

NR-970.title: DECISION TAKEN: how the shelf spoils (BL-1179)
NR-970.source: the sprint 49 main session (Ben: "I'll also trust your judgement"; NR-968 brought spoilage forward)

NR-971.title: CALL: where does a habitable world's water come from? (BL-1198)
NR-971.what: Water deposits are seeded on icy substrate only (RESOURCES.md:147). On an earthlike home body that puts all extractable water at the poles, far from the people who bid for it, so household water, clean water and medical supplies go unsupplied on most seeds (no water extractor at all on seeds 10/11/13/37). Every other sprint 49 fix (routing, placement, scorer, households eating, spoilage) leaves this untouched.

options: A: a Well / pumping station - an extraction site gated on adjacency to fresh water (river or lake), as the Fishing Wharf is gated on coast; cities on rivers drink
B: groundwater - every habitable land tile holds a small water deposit, scaled by habitability or rainfall

D: other

It follows the Fishing Wharf precedent (adjacency-gated extraction, no new deposit field), it is a deterministic consequence of terrain generation already has (rivers, lakes), and it is legible: where the river runs, water is cheap - which makes river cities matter, a Trade-shaped consequence.

Written into PRODUCTION.md sec Extraction buildings and RESOURCES.md; the work is BL-1198 (water where people live).

B: ratify k = 1 as measured
C: other

NR-977.title: DECISION TAKEN: a short shelf is shared within each phase of the tick, construction first (BL-1209)
NR-977.what: Your pro-rata ruling says every draw admitted against a short shelf in a tick shares it. The tick draws in phases: construction sites draw before labour is solved, processors after. Pooling both phases into one ration would mean reordering the tick, so the share is computed within each phase: sites share among themselves, then processors share what is left; upkeep draws stay first-come after both. A short steel shelf can therefore go to sites before plants. MARKETS.md will say so exactly.
NR-977.why_it_matters: Construction-first can starve production of a shared input in a tight market; the alternative is a tick reorder.
options: A: keep per-phase, construction first
B: pool the phases (reorder the tick so sites and plants share one ration)
C: per-phase, production first
NR-977.recommendation: A for sprint 49; revisit in sprint 50 (logistics) if the trade-flow lens shows sites starving plants.
NR-977.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-26 (sprint 57 close review form): accepted as taken.

NR-1049.title: BL-1352 (one LP system): three readings taken so a march could draw the nation's pool
NR-1049.what: The march now draws Logistic Points and claims ahead of production. Four readings the doc does not settle, each cheap to change. (1) WHOSE POOL - THE MOVER'S. A corporation's march draws its HOME NATION's points, a nation's garrison its own; never the pool of the ground it stands on. The first cut read the ground's nation and a cold review caught both consequences: a unit whose points ran out on unowned wilderness could never be granted again (a refusal moves nothing, so it re-fired for ever and the unit was stranded for good), and a unit invading another nation drew ITS VICTIM's pool, starving the defender's industry to fund the attack. LOGISTICS.md's 'Movement a player or rival DIRECTS' is the reading taken. The alternative - the ground's nation, with a stranding escape and a foreign-ground rule - is a real design and is Ben's if he wants it. (2) NO REACH TEST ON A MARCH - a unit draws its own nation's pool at full strength wherever it stands, because the off-network military reach is still 'military detail later' (LOGISTICS.md). (3) THE CLAIM IS GATHERED BEFORE THE BATTLE PHASE - the resolve runs at tick phase 4 and the march at phase 11, with battles at 10, so a unit killed in battle has already consumed its nation's points for that tick; the alternative is resolving the pool twice a tick. (4) THE EXCHANGE RATE IS UNCHANGED - one point admits one march-point of movement (infantry 1.0, cavalry 1.5 a tick) against a production need of 10 per unit of run, so a 50-unit army asks for ~60 points of a pool measured in the hundreds. Nothing measured says a soldier-tick and a unit of grain burden a nation equally; the old per-anchor rate (20/tick at every city) carried the same assumption.
NR-1049.why_it_matters: Reading 4 decides whether 'guns, butter and freight compete in one currency' is felt at all: at these numbers a march is a rounding error against production, which is the opposite of the campaign-starves-its-industry cost the doc describes. Reading 1 is the one that changes what a war looks like - who pays for an invasion's logistics. The 2040 spectator run is the measurement that should settle 4.
NR-1049.call: Accept the four, or name the one to move - most likely the march's weight (4), once the 2040 run shows what an army actually costs a nation.
NR-1049.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the sprint 55 close form): (1) the mover's own nation pays, as built. (4) the 1:1 exchange rate is kept as settled, not as a reading awaiting the 2040 measurement. Readings (2) and (3) stand as built.

(2) TERRAIN: the leg is multiplied by the tile's own traversal weight, so crossing a mountain or open water costs proportionally more than crossing a field. The doc says 'per tile' and is silent on terrain; a flat leg would price an unroaded island tile three steps across the sea exactly as a field three steps across a meadow, which a cold review flagged as the one place the walk ignores a domain every other cost walk in the tree respects.

NR-1050.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the sprint 55 close forms): keep 3.0 x terrain for market attraction, as built. The leg prices catchment only and moves no Logistic Points; off the networks, points supply units alone. Written into LOGISTICS.md section 3b.

NR-1073.title: Construction from placement: the first clearing pays two quarters at once, and more sites stall
NR-1073.source: Construction-in-days lane (c7e2b818, merged 6322792b), construction_stall vs main 2967c7cf
NR-1073.what: Per your ruling, a site builds on credit from its placement day, and its first clearing pays the credit days plus the quarter ahead. Sites stalled 10+ ticks: 51/81/78 against 32/23/72, and the stall verdicts move from short to contended. Two mechanisms in the code, neither yet isolated by measurement: (1) the credit rate reads the shelf as it stands and reserves nothing, so every site placed in one tick reads the same stock and all get full rate; (2) at the next clearing each owes 90 days in arrears plus 90 ahead, and one rate throttles both, so a short shelf slows the work ahead as well as the debt.
NR-1073.why_it_matters: A build that should finish a quarter sooner can finish later, because the lumped first draw meets a contended shelf. The ruling is honoured as written; the open question is how the debt competes with the work ahead.
options: A) Ahead first: the clearing sets the rate on the quarter ahead alone, and pays arrears only from what is left. The debt carries forward until paid; a building may complete still owing it.
B) Reserve on credit: a credit site claims its share of the shelf, so later placements in the same tick read what is left. This keeps the lumped draw but stops the over-promise.
C) Keep as built, and record the stall figures as the cost of the ruling.

A tick never draws two quarters of materials. A site cancelled before completion refunds its credit cost in full (Ben, 2026-10-25); materials already drawn stay spent.

NR-1083.title: May rival nations use fronts?

NR-1083.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-27: A — rivals assign their own units to their own fronts and choose hold or push. Written as a grant in AI_OPPONENT.md § 11 and in MILITARY.md § Fronts.

NR-1092.title: Fronts: the calls taken on your behalf
NR-1092.what: Slots: unit i of n takes span[(2i+1)L/2n]; "on slot" is the slot tile's province. A hand march on an assigned unit is overridden by its front; unassign to march by hand. Push enters the neighbour's adjacent land province with the least summed unit strength. Re-anchor keeps a key only while it faces the same neighbour, else the nearest front toward that neighbour, else drops. Rivals assign only idle units outside their capital province (the capital garrison stays home), to the front with fewest units per span tile, and push only when hostile and stronger 3:2. A push the march refuses holds instead.
